chapter_theme: Mounachiddhar's kuravanji: twelve stanzas in the first person plural, a company of Siddhars declaring what they have done and will do. They subdue the ego, seek the guru's and the Lord's feet by Manonmani's grace, bind the breath, kindle the fire at the root, sit in a mountain cave on kalpa without food or sleep, see the supreme open space and the light beyond the ninety-six tattvas, refuse kin, the sinful and the world's doings, and end with the 'I' of anava cut and tapas held as the only refuge.
structure_note: The stanzas are rhymed quatrains of vows (-வோம், -ந்தோம்), without a refrain. 2235 to 2239 give the devotional frame (light, Manonmani, the guru, elders, the thousand Siddhars); 2240 to 2245 the yogic method and its sights (breath, root fire, cave, nose-tip, the shakti-wheel, paraveli); 2246 closes on the ego cut away. The verb shifts once to the singular (2245 அறிந்து கொண்டேன் யானே, 2246 விடுத்தேன்).

2235.reading: Seeking the great primal light every day, singing to win the grace of the Lord's feet, receiving the grace of Manonmani who is light, and holding in the mind the feet of Sukar.
2235.nuance: The stanza is all participles and finishes in the next one, so it is a frame rather than a claim. சுகருடைய பாதம் may name the sage Suka as the poet's guru-line, or mean simply the feet of the blissful one; tradition often counts Suka among the Siddhars' teachers. Manonmani is the Shakti of the mind's transcendence, named again in 2239.

2236.reading: Subduing pride and looking to the state of grace, setting the mind to know all the rare worlds, we will bow duly at the feet of the great, and practise yogic absorption with devotion every day.
2236.nuance: ஆங்காரம், the ego as a faculty (ahankara), heads the chapter as it closes it in 2246. Devotion and yoga-nishtha are paired without strain: the kuravanji makes no quarrel between bhakti and method.

2237.reading: Was it not by burning the ghost's nature that we saw the Brahma-state? Passing beyond Brahma's seat we took our place in the sushumna; not roaming like a dog, we stayed in tapas, having subdued the ego well and with dignity.
2237.nuance: பிரமநிலை and பிரமபதி may be Brahman (the Supreme state) or Brahma the creator, whose seat in the yogic map is a lower centre; on the second reading the stanza is coded, the breath passing Brahma's centre and entering the central channel. நல்லதொரு ஆங்காரம், a 'good' ego that is subdued, is odd; the sense may be that even the good self-regard is held down.

2238.reading: Trusting the deceitful life, we will not fall into anxieties; we will not tire of seeking the feet of the great sages; we will never look at those guilty of the five great sins; we will not forget the friendship of those who have cut off the bond of sinful deeds.
2238.nuance: The stanza is about company: whom to seek, whom to refuse. பஞ்சமா பாதகர் are the doers of the five great sins of the dharma texts (traditionally killing, theft, drink, adultery and keeping such company).

2239.reading: Singing every day with a thousand Siddhars, we will dance the holy dance of bliss together; knowing the siddhi that Mother Uma Manonmani told me, we will live by it, keeping close to the great.
2239.nuance: The Siddhars here are a company, a thousand who sing and dance, not solitary adepts. The teaching comes from the goddess, not from a human guru, but is to be lived out beside the elders. சித்தை could be the siddhi or simply the wisdom she spoke.

2240.reading: Melting and pining in thought to find the state, seeking daily the feet of the stainless Lord, knowing the kala we seized the breath and bound it; raising the fire, we read the root with ease.
2240.nuance: கலை here is probably the breath's phase (the moon and sun channels), and வாசி the breath as practice; கனல் எழுப்பி மூலமதை is taken by tradition as kindling the fire at the muladhara, the waking of kundalini. 'Read the root' (படித்தோம்) is the coded verb: to master or know the root centre.

2241.reading: Giving up food and sleep we practised yogic absorption; cutting off our kin we lived in a mountain cave; we saw the supreme space that sight cannot reach; eating kalpa we grew the body.
2241.nuance: The stanza holds together the two aims the Siddhars refuse to separate: the vision of the open (பரவெளி) and a body made to last by kalpa, the rejuvenating preparation. It claims the body was grown, not escaped.

2242.reading: We will not languish in fond dealings with father, mother and kin; we will not seek works that do not reach and know the state of tapas; we knew jnana in wonder, as the highest thing, and knew the grace of the supreme space.
2242.nuance: The second line is compressed: செய்கை may be any outward work, or the rites, that fails to reach tapas. The refusal of parents and kin repeats 2241 and is the kuravanji's plainest renunciation.

2243.reading: We learned to fix the gaze along the tip of the nose; we knew the whirl of the good root-circle; knowing how to raise the breath, we will cut off desires, and refuse without fail the doings of the world.
2243.nuance: நாசிநுனி, the nose-tip gaze, and மூலவட்டம் சுழி, the whirl of the root circle, are technical body-places; tradition takes the whirl as the coil at the base where the central channel begins. The point is causal: raising the breath is what cuts desire.

2244.reading: Climbing the seat of the shakti-wheel we saw the pure open; holding in mind that all is the supreme open, we will know every day the freed ones who gained siddhi, and come to know with attention what the life-kala is.
2244.nuance: சக்திசக்ர பீடம் is probably one of the body's centres, the seat of Shakti, and சீவகலை the digit or phase of the life, perhaps the moon-kala of the breath; both are coded and their places are not given. The stanza moves from a sight (space seen) to a view (all is space).

2245.reading: We took in what is told of the ninety-six tattvas; in the supreme open we saw the Lord's feet; I came to know what heaven is, seeing for myself the light of the supreme open.
2245.nuance: The ninety-six tattvas are the Siddhars' fuller count of the body's constituents, against the thirty-six of the Saiva texts. உரைத்தனங்களைக் கொண்டோம் is unclear: 'took the accounts of' or 'passed through'. விண்ணுலகு, heaven, is here something seen within, not a place after death.

2246.reading: I cut away with relish the anava that says 'I'; gaining the good, I came to live in a cave; we came having quelled the pride that says 'self'; holding tapas alone as the way, we delighted in the path of the breath.
2246.nuance: ஆணவம் is the first of the malas, the bond of 'I'; the stanza names it and cuts it with a light word (நயந்து, gladly). சரவழி is the path of the breath (சரம், svara), so even the closing tapas is breath-practice.

links.note: Tirumular nurtured the body because without it true knowledge cannot be won; Mounachiddhar's company ate kalpa and grew the body in the same cave where they saw the supreme open. Both make the lasting body a means of the vision, not its enemy.

One poet laments that by not keeping his eyes on the nose-tip his body was spoiled and his understanding lost; Mounachiddhar's Siddhars learned the nose-tip gaze and with it cut off desire. The same practice, its loss and its keeping.

Tirumular turns the one who blazes at the root opening upward with the breath joined; Mounachiddhar seizes the breath and raises the fire at the root. The same coupling of breath and root-fire, here told as a thing the company has done.

source_issues: 2245 தய்யபர வெளி is probably a corrupt form (perhaps தெய்வ or தூய); உரைத்தனங்களை is unclear.
2235 is grammatically incomplete and runs into 2236; it reads as the opening frame of the poem.
